page: Microsoft Azure D96ps_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the ARM64 architecture, powered by 96 dedicated physical cores of the 3.4 GHz Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor. It features 384.0 GB of memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache, with hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES. The configuration operates without simultaneous multithreading, allocating one thread per core directly under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance includes no onboard GPU accelerators and no bundled local storage, requiring external attached storage volumes.

In multi-threaded computational workloads, the server demonstrates top-tier performance, achieving top-decile scores in stress-ng multi-core tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Clang compilation benchmarks. Its memory subsystem registers top-tier bandwidth, exceeding 464 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and over 10,800 GB/sec for cached small-block operations. In-memory data structures perform effectively, registering 169.79 million Redis SET operations per second and 103.34 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Single-thread performance falls within the middle 50% across Geekbench and stress-ng evaluations, reflecting an architectural prioritization of parallel core density over peak single-core clock speeds.

The absence of local scratch disks necessitates reliance on external network-attached volumes for persistent data. From a resource efficiency standpoint, the provision of 96 dedicated physical ARM cores eliminates noisy-neighbor core contention, translating to predictable throughput across horizontally scaled tasks. Microsoft Azure D96ps_v6 is suited for large-scale distributed compilation pipelines, high-concurrency web serving tiers, in-memory caching systems such as Redis, batch data processing, and enterprise application hosting.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ps_v6 is an ARM64-based general-purpose instance featuring 96 dedicated physical cores powered by 3.4 GHz Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processors and 384.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping, it lacks local storage and bundled GPU accelerators, utilizing remote storage volumes. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier multi-threaded processing, high memory bandwidth reaching 464.33 GB/sec on uncached reads, and exceptional throughput across Redis SET operations (169.79 million ops/sec) and static web serving (103.34 GB/sec). While single-core speeds remain in the median tier, its high physical core count delivers stable parallel throughput without hyperthreading overhead. The instance is designed for high-concurrency web tiers, software compilation pipelines, in-memory caching, and parallelized enterprise workloads.
